subject: Staggered MAP & eval -> commit plan for GPU pool (FinServe)
messages:
From: Logan Kim <logank@finserve.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Staggered MAP & eval -> commit plan for GPU pool

Evelyn / Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. FinServe wants to move from evaluation to a staged commitment but needs the commercial terms tied to a mutual action plan (MAP) so our legal/procurement stakeholders can sign off. High-level ask:

- Pilot / eval: 30-day evaluation window (we'll run production-ish loads)
- Initial pool: equivalent of 12 A100 GPUs (mixed instance shapes ok) for months 0–2
- Ramp: step to 24 GPUs by month 3, then to 36 by month 6, to 48 by month 9 — all tied to MAP milestones (traffic/perf success metrics)
- Term: target 18 months preferred by procurement, but flexible if economics line up
- Burst: ability to burst 2x baseline for short windows (emergency and traffic spikes). Need clarity on burst pricing and approval flow

Can you send a short MAP draft with milestone checkpoints, proposed commit curve and pricing tiers, and a SOW we can push through procurement? Attaching our sizing workbook and a skeleton milestone tracker for context.

Attachments: GPU_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx; MAP_Milestones_Tracker.csv

Target close: our CFO would like a signed agreement by ~Dec 10 if we can get procurement what they need. Can your team hit that?

—Logan
VP, Platform Engineering
FinServe
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Kim <logank@finserve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staggered MAP & eval -> commit plan for GPU pool

Logan — thanks, this is helpful and realistic. I've sketched a short MAP and pricing outline below so your procurement and engineering teams have concrete checkpoints to review. I'll attach a draft SOW as well; Marissa is looping on the commercial redlines.

Proposed MAP (high-level):
- Eval (0–30 days): Dedicated pilot pool equal to 12 GPU eq. Redwood provides $12k in credits for inference tokens and 3 engineering hours of onboarding support.
- Milestone A (by end of month 2): throughput >= 80% of target QPS on production traces — unlock 24-GPU commit (month 3 onwards).
- Milestone B (month 4): 95th-pct latency < target; unlock 36-GPU commit (month 6 onwards).
- Milestone C (month 8): sustained utilization > 60% over 14 days; unlock full 48-GPU commit (month 9 onwards).

Pricing / commitment sketch (examples):
- Initial 12-GPU pilot (month 0–2): discounted pilot rate = $X/hour per GPU equivalent; billing converts to committed credit if project moves to paid service before day 30.
- Staggered commit tiers: commit to stepped GPU-months (we'll produce a commit schedule in the SOW). Example discounts: 8% at 12-GPU baseline, 12% once you hit 24-GPU committed floor, 18% at 48-GPU committed floor (term-dependent).
- Term options: 12-month or 18-month; 18-month yields +3% on top of listed discounts.

Burst rules (proposal):
- Emergency burst (ad hoc): up to 2x baseline for up to 2 hours/day, billed at on-demand per-GPU rate above committed capacity. First 4 emergency bursts per quarter are waived.
- Scheduled planned burst: pre-approved (24h notice) can be covered under burst pool credits with a fixed uplift (example +25% unit price during burst).

Next steps:
1) Marissa sends a commercial redline with explicit dollar figures and a formal discount ladder.
2) Rishi and I will convert the MAP into SOW milestones that tie to commit activation.
3) We'll share a DocuSign link so procurement can review and route.

Attaching: FinServe_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (first pass)

Can the team confirm whether the proposed emergency burst waiver count (4/quarter) and the 2-hour/day cap are acceptable? Also confirm preferred term (12v18 months). If procurement is aiming for Dec 10 signature, we'll prioritize an executable SOW and a short commercial summary.

Thanks — Evelyn
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Park <alicia.park@finserve.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staggered MAP & eval -> commit plan for GPU pool

Evelyn — appreciate the clear framing. A few procurement questions and constraints from my side:

1) FinServe procurement prefers an 18-month economic term, but we need the discount ladder and exact $/GPU-hour numbers to run TCO. Can you provide a simple excel with committed vs on-demand unit prices by tier?

2) Burst: procurement will not accept open-ended automatic burst. We need a gating mechanism: emergency bursts OK (with waiver count), but any scheduled or recurring burst must require a change request and approval from our SRE lead. The +25% uplift for scheduled burst is acceptable if there's a cap on monthly burst spend (we propose 15% of monthly committed spend).

3) We also need to see language for data isolation and audit logs in the SOW — our security team will triage.

Procurement timeline: if you can deliver exact unit prices and a clean SOW by Dec 4 EOD, we can do internal routing and target Dec 10 signature. Otherwise it'll slip another week.

—Alicia
Director, Procurement (FinServe)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Park <alicia.park@finserve.com>, Logan Kim <logank@finserve.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staggered MAP & eval -> commit plan for GPU pool

Alicia / Logan —

Thanks — posted a concise commercial redline below (will attach a unit-price matrix in a follow-up Excel):

Commercial redline (summary):
- Unit pricing (example): committed GPU-equivalent hour = $3.40 (12-GPU floor), on-demand = $6.20. Exact numbers in spreadsheet to follow.
- Discount ladder (applies to committed spend): 8% discount at 12-GPU equivalent, 12% at 24-GPU, 18% at 48-GPU. For 18-month term, add an incremental 3% off committed spend (stacked).
- Convert pilot charges: any pilot usage during eval converts into committed credits if you execute the SOW within 30 days of pilot start (credit applied to month-1 invoice).
- Burst pricing: emergency bursts billed at on-demand rates; first four emergency bursts/quarter waived. Scheduled bursts: +25% uplift on committed unit price but capped at 15% of monthly committed invoice unless approved by change request.
- Early termination: pro-rated refund of unused committed credits after 90 days, with a 60-day wind-down service fee (we can include explicit numbers in SOW).

We will:
- Attach a unit price matrix and commit schedule by EOD Dec 4.
- Update SOW to include the isolation/audit log language for the deployment model (customer-managed VPC option and KMS integration note).

If Dec 10 signature is still the goal, please confirm that procurement can accept the +3% 18-month incentivized model versus a deeper upfront discount. We can bake in a one-time onboarding credit to sweeten month-1 economics if that helps close.

—Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Logan Kim <logank@finserve.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Staggered MAP & eval -> commit plan for GPU pool

Marissa / Evelyn —

This looks workable. Procurement is comfortable with the gating approach on scheduled bursts and the 18-month term +3% incentive trade is reasonable. Two asks before we route to signatures:

1) Final unit-price matrix (spreadsheet) with committed vs on-demand rows so our finance team can sign off.
2) A DocuSign SOW link and an explicit close checklist (who signs, approximate routing time).

If we get both by EOD Dec 6 we should be able to meet the Dec 10 target. Please send the DocuSign link when ready and we'll queue finance/procurement.

Thanks — Logan
VP, Platform Engineering
FinServe
